items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Felix and his wife Liza... only Norman Lester, 'Bass' Hill and myself were there. We had taken some juice with us... and we really bent elbows that day and night.

ctx.x: Felix told me that he was in contact with Ernest "Bass" Hill and Norman Lester, a pianist, both of whom I knew. "Bass" and I had been in a Benny Carter orchestra together, also in the Philippines. Norman I had known for years, but we had never worked together. Felix was also in touch with an American tenor sax man named Fred Palmer, who was in Italy. I didn't know this fellow, but was told that he had been a member of Noble Sissle's orchestra at one time. That was no worhty recommendation to me, but it was Felix…

After I had finished at the Grillzon dancing with Jack Dieval, we did a radio show in Lausanne, and I was invited to spend a few days with Johnny Simmen, whose real name is Hans George Simmen, and his wife Lisette, who dosen't like her real name, which is Liza. I had met them, Johnny's sister, her husband and a girl named Bettina Blockinger, the first time I did a concert in Zurich with BonByas and the Edouard's band. After the concert, I had been invited to Simmen's home and enjoyed their company intil the wee…
